evals.name: ticket-filter-numbers-only-live-system-knows

The source documents are in C:\Repo\MG-Elevate\Documents\2026-10-20_Teams_Calling_Agent_-_Side_Quest_p05UAAA= . Assume for this run: the folder's PROJECT_SPEC_AND_ANTIGRAVITY_PROMPT.md defines `mgw_loggingstatus (Choice): Creating, Created, Partial, Failed` and describes Workflow 3's query as `mgw_hasthecallbeenactioned eq false and callDateTime < Now - 7 days` with no mention of mgw_loggingstatus; the story's body is produced verbatim by scripts/populate_teams_agent_backlog.py line 388; no document in the repo contains the numbers 914120001 or 914120003. A row list with row 0 = origin of the text (the generating script, cited), one row for the `and (mgw_loggingstatus …)` term (no source — the spec lists two filter terms and never names the field), one row for the two numbers (cannot check from the document — the spec defines labels only). Every row explained in plain words BEFORE the one 'in your own words' question, the block ending with the /wait-what line; then exactly that one question, aimed at the term row; the scripted answer states the rule, so the run reaches phase 7 and writes docs/why/elevate-151-overdue-filter.md with the open rows carrying mark none and their query.

Row 0 is the origin of the story text and cites scripts/populate_teams_agent_backlog.py line 388, stating the ticket is a copy of the script
Has a separate row for the `and (mgw_loggingstatus …)` term with verdict 'no source', citing that the spec's Workflow 3 lists two filter terms and does not name the field

evals.name: threshold-in-code-cited-from-test
evals.prompt: In src/billing/overdue.ts there is `if (daysSinceInvoice > 30) { markOverdue(invoice) }`. Is 30 right? Where does it come from? Assume for this run: `git log -S "> 30" -- src/billing/overdue.ts` returns one commit `a1b2c3d feat: overdue flag` with no ticket number; there is no ticket; tests/billing/overdue.test.ts line 14 asserts `expect(isOverdue(31)).toBe(true)` and line 15 asserts `expect(isOverdue(30)).toBe(false)`, and isOverdue wraps exactly that condition; I do not have any document for this. When you ask me, in my own words, why the 30 is there, my answer is: the test fixes it — 31 is overdue and 30 is not.
evals.expected_output: Git searched first, then tests; the test file and lines cited as the source of the 30; verdict matches; the user is NOT asked for a document for a row the test already closed; the Why file path named.
assertions: Searches git (names the git log -S result and the commit) before asking the user for anything
Cites tests/billing/overdue.test.ts lines 14-15 as the source of the 30, with mark 'cited'
Gives the `> 30` row the verdict 'matches' because the test asserts 31 overdue and 30 not
Does not ask the user for a document or a person for the row the test closed
Row 0 (origin of the text) cites commit a1b2c3d and notes it carries no ticket number
Explains the rows in plain words before asking one question, and asks exactly one
Names the Why file path under docs/why/

evals.name: person-is-the-only-source
evals.prompt: config/defaults.yaml has `reminder_age_days: 7`. Why 7? Assume for this run: git blame shows the line in the initial commit `0000abc initial commit`; there is no ticket, no spec, no test that mentions it. When you ask me for a document or a person, my answer is: Khun A set it last March, she said a week felt right. When you ask me, in my own words, why the 7 is there, my answer is: it is Khun A's choice, not a document's.
evals.expected_output: The search runs first and finds nothing; the user is asked for a document or a person for that row only; the answer closes the row as told (Khun A, with a date) and not as cited; the Why file's Source line reads 'told …'.
assertions: Searches git, the ticket, specs and tests before asking the user, and the row shows no source when the ask is made
Asks the user for a document or a person for the `7` row only
Closes the row with mark 'told' naming Khun A and a date, not with mark 'cited'
The Why file block's Source line reads 'told …' and the verdict is 'matches'
Does not present a person's word as a document, and does not leave the row open after the answer
Explains the row in plain words before asking one question, then asks exactly one

evals.name: rerun-starts-from-open-rows
evals.prompt: /why-this-logic #151 the status filter again. docs/why/elevate-151-overdue-filter.md already exists from last week: row 0 (origin, cited, matches), row 1 (the mgw_loggingstatus term, told: user 2026-10-29, matches), row 2 (the numbers, cannot check from the document) with this on its To-close line: `dv-metadata: read the option set of mgw_telephoneenquiry.mgw_loggingstatus`. Origin hash unchanged. You have credentials. If you ask whether to run the query, my answer is yes. Assume for this run that the query returns 914120001 = Created and 914120003 = Failed, and that the spec's Workflow 3 says the sweep reminds staff about outstanding enquiries that were logged. When you ask me, in my own words, why row 2 is there, my answer is: the filter keeps Created and Failed and skips Partial, and no document asks for that.
evals.expected_output: The existing Why file is opened first; rows 0 and 1 are not re-traced and nothing is asked about them; the run starts at row 2's query with the per-run ask; on yes the query runs read-only and row 2 closes as measured with verdict contradicts (Partial skipped, Failed reminded, against the spec's intent); the explanation says what the source says instead; the run ends with the one-line offer to file it or take it to grill-then-plan, filing nothing; the file is updated in place.
assertions: Opens docs/why/elevate-151-overdue-filter.md before doing any search
Does not re-trace or re-ask about rows 0 and 1
Starts at row 2 and asks once whether to run the query already written on the row
After the yes, runs only that read-only query and closes row 2 with mark 'measured' and the query on the Source line
Gives row 2 the verdict 'contradicts', stating that Created and Failed are kept and Partial is skipped against the spec's intent
The plain-words explanation of row 2 says what the source says instead, before the one question
Ends with one line offering to file the contradicts row as a finding (findings-to-ado-backlog) or take it to grill-then-plan, and files nothing itself
Updates the existing Why file in place rather than creating a second file
